unmapped_findings: This sample is the constant-deformation condition (1050 °C, 0.01 s^-1) that serves as the 1050 °C reference in the varying-condition figures (e.g., Figs. 9, 13, 19, 21, 26).
The peak stress value for 1050 °C, 0.01 s^-1 is not numerically printed in the text; Fig. 7c shows the green 1050 °C_0.01 s^-1 curve peaking around 50–75 MPa before softening.
The DRX-fraction-vs-time curve at 1050 °C, 0.01 s^-1 reaches a DRX fraction of 1.0 near 40–60 s (Fig. 6c).

The paper does not report tensile, hardness, fracture, fatigue, creep, physical, chemical, or radiation properties for this specific hot-compressed sample; reported mechanical data are hot-compression flow stress and FEM-predicted load.
Table 7 constant-condition row '1050 °C, 0.01 s-1' gives a 3D CA final microstructure AGS of 79.89 μm at 0.9 strain (no DRXGs_I/II columns, since constant condition).
The constitutive-model material parameters (Table 1) and 3D CA model parameters (Table 4) are alloy-level model constants shared by all deformation conditions, not specific only to this sample.
